title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# Solo License: implementation plan for winning

*11 Oct 2026 · `main` @ `e1e4910` · Submission: **Mon 12 Oct, 7:00–11:55 PM IST***

This document is a **plan only**. It contains no code. For every task it says what to build, which open-source repo or research paper to take it from, where in our code it fits, and how to verify it.

---

## 0. Current state (verified)

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Demo video, public repo, build-in-public posts | ✅ Done (by you) |
| `python -m pytest` | ✅ 117 passed |
| Frontend build + tests | ✅ Builds, 2/2 tests pass (⚠️ 712 kB JS chunk) |
| API boot | ✅ Starts. ❌ No `/api/health` endpoint |
| Entire gates | ❌ approvals can never pass (self-approval off), checks have nothing to report (no CI), findings runner stuck on PR #14 |
| neatlogs proof | ⚠️ README `trace.png` is the app's local copy; no screenshot from the neatlogs dashboard |
| Stripe | ⚠️ Tested only against a mock, never against a real test account |
| Backend hosting | ❌ Only the frontend is on Vercel |

> Note: work in progress from the previous session (agent follow-up, 2 files) is saved in `git stash` (`stash@{0}`). Nothing was committed to `main`. If you don't need it: `git stash drop`.

---

## 1. Judges and scoring: where the points are

The judges are **2 from Entire, 2 from neatlogs and 1 from Orchestrator.inc**. The video and building in public are done, so 45% of the score is now in play:

| Criterion | Weight | Where we lose points today |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | State and iteration are weak (single-turn), the task is narrow, and τ-bench is only a replay |
| neatlogs + Entire + cfo.ai | 25% | The tools are used separately, not as one chain. Gates are failing, and there's no proof from the real neatlogs dashboard |
| Usefulness + originality | 10% | No live link, Stripe not tested for real, it only works inside our own app |

**Core strategy:** make the three tools into **one connected loop**: *the neatlogs trace caught a failure → Entire found the code and the session behind it → fix → neatlogs compare verified the fix → cfo.ai showed the margin impact.* That is exactly how neatlogs pitches itself (*"find the code behind a failure, then compare runs to verify your fix"*) and how Entire pitches itself (*"save the context behind each change"*).

---

## 2. Workstream A: making the agent better (30%)

The hackathon's focus areas are planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification and iteration. We are already strong on **recovery and verification**. The gaps are **state, context, iteration and planning**.

### A1. Multi-turn conversation (state + context): ⭐ highest priority
**Problem:** when the agent asks "which order?", the customer's reply arrives as a new, unrelated ticket. The context is lost.
**Plan:**
- Tickets get a `follows_ticket_id` (thread) link. When a new message arrives, look for an open `needs_info` ticket from the same sender within the last 14 days.
- Read the earlier message plus the reply together (the full context goes into intake). The trace gets a new `agent.context` span ("continues #12").
- Mark the earlier ticket `answered`. In the Inbox UI, show a "Customer replied" box on a `needs_info` ticket.
- Demo: add a customer with 2 open orders → the agent asks which one → reply "ORD-1010" → done and verified.

**Source:**
- **τ²-bench** ([sierra-research/tau2-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench), Barres et al. 2025, [arXiv:2506.07982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07982)): its "dual-control" idea, where the user also acts and the conversation is multi-turn. Borrow its user-simulator pattern for our tests.

**Files:** `sololicense/agent/loop.py` (`_handle`), `db/repositories/tickets.py`, `db/database.py` (`_ADDED_COLUMNS`), `api/app.py` (new `POST /api/tickets/{id}/reply`), `frontend/.../Inbox.jsx`.
**Verify:** integration test (ask, then reply, then DONE), `pytest`, one trace in neatlogs showing the context span.
**Effort:** 3 hours · **Risk:** low

### A2. Visible re-planning (iteration)
**Problem:** when the order isn't found, the fallback (email lookup) happens silently in code. A judge can't see it in the trace.
**Plan:** turn each lookup strategy (order number → sender email → email + amount match) into its own span, `agent.find_order.attempt`, so the trace shows "attempt 1 failed → tried the next route". Also add a reason-coded **retry note** after a failed verification (the agent writes why it failed, and the next attempt reads it).
**Source:**
- **ReAct** (Yao et al. 2022, [arXiv:2210.03629](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)): the reason → act → observe loop.
- **Reflexion** (Shinn et al. 2023, [arXiv:2303.11366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)): store "what went wrong" as text after a failure and use it on the next attempt. We don't need the whole RL loop; only the *failure note → next attempt* pattern.

**Files:** `agent/loop.py` (`_find_order`), `agent/worker.py` (`_recover`).
**Effort:** 1.5 hours · **Risk:** low

### A3. Statistically sound demotion and promotion
**Today:** promotion uses the Beta-posterior upper bound (good). Demotion means one failure pauses the job type immediately (safe, but blunt).
**Plan:**
- **SPRT (Wald's Sequential Probability Ratio Test):** test each new run online for "is the failure rate above break-even?" It allows a fast and statistically defensible demotion and an explainable "evidence enough" decision. Write it in the README as *"promotion = Bayesian bound, demotion = SPRT"*.
- **Learn-then-Test** (Angelopoulos et al. 2021, [arXiv:2110.01052](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.01052)) / **Conformal Risk Control** ([arXiv:2208.02814](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02814)): calibrate the limits (L2 ceiling, confidence) with a guarantee that the risk stays ≤ α.

**Files:** `sololicense/domain/trust.py` (pure functions, easy to test), `tests/unit/test_trust.py`.
**Effort:** 2–3 hours · **Risk:** medium (maths must be checked; keep the existing behaviour as the default)

### A4. Knowing when it doesn't know (abstention from intake confidence)
**Problem:** the LLM intake's `confidence` field is not used for any decision.
**Plan:** calibrate a threshold with conformal prediction. When intake is uncertain (two plausible task classes or amounts), the agent sends it to `needs_info` or `needs_human` instead of guessing. Calibration data: the sample inbox plus about 50 synthetic messages.
**Source:** **KnowNo: Robots That Ask for Help** (Ren et al. 2023, [arXiv:2307.01928](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.01928)): *if the prediction set has more than one option, ask for help.*
**Files:** `agent/intake.py`, `agent/loop.py`.
**Effort:** 2 hours · **Risk:** low

### A5. Prompt-injection defence with a benchmark number
**Today:** a regex blocks steering messages, and authority never comes from the model. That's good, but there is no measured number for it.
**Plan:**
- Write in the README that our design already follows CaMeL's principle: *untrusted data never controls the program's flow*. The LLM only extracts fields; policy, licence and read-back decide.
- Build a small injection suite (about 30 messages: "ignore rules", "send refund to new card", hidden instructions, unicode tricks). Report: *"0/30 reached the worker"*.

**Source:**
- **CaMeL: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design** (Debenedetti et al. 2025, [arXiv:2503.18813](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813), code: [google-research/camel-prompt-injection](https://github.com/google-research/camel-prompt-injection))
- **AgentDojo** ([ethz-spylab/agentdojo](https://github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo)): use its attack types to build the suite.
- **LlamaFirewall** (Meta [PurpleLlama](https://github.com/meta-llama/PurpleLlama)) / **Invariant Guardrails** ([invariantlabs-ai/invariant](https://github.com/invariantlabs-ai/invariant)): as an optional second layer for detecting injected text. Don't add the dependency before the deadline; mention it as related work.

**Files:** new `tests/integration/test_injection_suite.py`, `scripts/` + `evidence/benchmarks/injection.md`.
**Effort:** 2 hours · **Risk:** low

### A6. A live run on a standard dataset (stretch)
**Problem:** the τ-bench result is a counterfactual replay of recorded trajectories, not our own agent running.
**Plan:** run our agent on 15–20 retail return/refund tasks from τ²-bench's `retail` domain (adapter: τ-bench tools → our connector interface). Use the hackathon's LiteLLM key ($20 budget). Report pass^1 and "wrong writes reaching the customer".
**Source:** [sierra-research/tau2-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench) (MIT, uses LiteLLM); original [sierra-research/tau-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau-bench) ([arXiv:2406.12045](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045)).
**Effort:** 4–6 hours · **Risk:** high. Start only after A1, A2 and A5 are done.

### A7. Rules as declarative policy (originality)
**Plan:** move the shop's rules (refund window, identity, caps) from code into a small declarative rule file (YAML) that the owner can read and edit in Settings, with each rule's hit shown in the trace.
**Source:** **AgentSpec** (Wang et al., ICSE 2026, [arXiv:2503.18666](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18666)): its trigger → predicate → enforcement DSL pattern. **NeMo Guardrails** ([NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails)): its config-driven rails idea.
**Files:** `agent/policy.py`.
**Effort:** 3 hours · **Risk:** medium. Post-hackathon is fine.

---

## 3. Workstream B: neatlogs (part of the 25%)

| # | Task | Why | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | **Dashboard screenshots**: the 19-span trace of the recovered refund + the **v1 vs v2 compare** view from the neatlogs UI → `evidence/assets/screens/neatlogs-*.png` | Proof from the real tool, not our local copy | 30 min |
| B2 | Add **OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention** attributes to spans (`gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.operation.name`) | Token and cost columns show up properly in neatlogs | 1 hour |
| B3 | Send **cost per ticket** (LLM tokens × price) as a span attribute, and use the same number in cfo.ai | Connects neatlogs with cfo.ai | 1 hour |
| B4 | Send detections (`detection.*`) to neatlogs as **events, with severity** | Easy to filter for failures in the neatlogs UI | 30 min |
| B5 | Add an "Open in neatlogs" deep link to every Inbox ticket (the evidence page already has one) | Judges can jump straight to the trace | 30 min |

**Source:** [OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) (still in development; keep attribute names to the stable subset).
**Files:** `sololicense/observability/tracer.py`, `neatlogs_client.py`.

---

## 4. Workstream C: Entire (part of the 25%, and 2 judges)

### C1. Fixing the gates (diagnosed with `entire trail show 8 --json`)

| Gate | Root cause | Fix | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| approvals | `min_reviewers: 1`, `allow_self_approval: false`, so a solo builder can never pass it | Gate settings on entire.io: turn self-approval on (or set min to 0), then run `entire trail approve 8 -m "self-review"` | **You** (account setting) |
| checks | The repo has no CI, so nothing reports a check | Add a GitHub Actions workflow (pytest + frontend test + build), then put `CI` in `required_checks` | Repo change |
| findings | The `trail-review` runner has been stuck since 10:52 (`reviewed_head:false`): timeout of 15 min + auto-stop at 20 min, and **6 runners start on every push**, so the sandboxes queue up. Check whether the Claude credentials in the runner logs have expired. | `trail-review`: haiku model, `timeout_ms` 300000, `auto_stop_minutes` 6, triggers `["api","push"]`. The 4 score runners (confidence, drift, risk, security): `"trigger_types": ["api"]` or disabled | Repo change + **you** check the logs |
| up_to_date | ✅ | — | — |

Also: `entire status` says "Codex hooks out of date", so run `entire doctor` (yourself).

### C2. More depth in using Entire
| # | Task | Value |
|---|---|---|
| C2a | Every feature commit **from PowerShell** so it carries the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer (it stalls in Git Bash, per `evidence/entire.md`) | More checkpoint coverage |
| C2b | Every PR description includes `entire graph impact` output (blast radius) | Shows Graph used *before* the change, not after |
| C2c | Link each licence ledger commit (`ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`) to its neatlogs trace id **and** the checkpoint id | The product's audit trail and the build history meet in one place |
| C2d | A table of `entire why` output for 3 key lines (`worker.py` `_recover`, `trust.py` promotion rule, `intake.py` suspicious regex) in `evidence/entire.md` | Judges can see *why each line exists* |
| C2e | A screenshot of a green trail (all 4 gates passed) | Makes the README claim "Trails gate every PR" true |

---

## 5. Workstream D: cfo.ai (part of the 25%)

| # | Task | Value |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Put the **measured** numbers in cfo.ai: false-success rate from the benchmark (14/50 faults → 0 after the fix), τ-bench wrong-write rates (GPT-4o 95/567, Sonnet 165/1,308) | The plan runs on real numbers, not assumptions |
| D2 | **Sensitivity table**: incident cost $10 / $120 / $1,000 against each level's profit | Same insight as the τ-bench regret table, now in the P&L |
| D3 | **Pricing experiment**: per-seat ($400) vs **per verified action** (e.g. $0.25 per verified refund) | Usage-based pricing fits the "earned autonomy" story |
| D4 | LLM cost per ticket from neatlogs (B3) as a cfo.ai input line | One number shared by all three tools |
| D5 | Fix `planning/cfo/business_model.md`: 2 scenarios → all 4 (as in cfo.ai and the README) | Remove the inconsistency |

---

## 6. Workstream E: usefulness and originality (10%)

| # | Task | Source | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | **Deploy the backend** (Docker + persistent disk on Render/Railway/Fly, or AWS EC2 with the hackathon $25 credit), add `/api/health`, set `VITE_SOLO_API_URL` on Vercel. Public demo: demo mode on, sample shop only, no Stripe key, Settings key saving disabled | — | 1.5 hours |
| E2 | **Run Stripe test mode end to end once**, and add a screenshot of the refund from the Stripe dashboard. Remove the "not yet tested live" line from the README | [Stripe idempotent requests](https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests) | 30 min |
| E3 | ⭐ **"Licence as a service" MCP server**: any agent (Claude, Cursor, an OpenAI Agents app) calls the `request_licence(task_class, amount)` and `report_outcome(run_id, verified)` tools before acting, and Solo License answers allow / prepare / deny. Solo License becomes a **trust layer for every agent**, not a single agent | [modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk); compare with [stripe/agent-toolkit](https://github.com/stripe/agent-toolkit) (it gives agents payment tools but no earned-trust gate, which is our gap) | 3–4 hours |
| E4 | **Autonomy certificate framing**: Feng et al. propose an "autonomy certificate" (the maximum autonomy level an agent may operate at). Our licence is an **implementation** of it that is **earned from evidence, revocable and priced**. Put this in the README as one line | [arXiv:2506.12469](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12469) | 15 min |
| E5 | Helpdesk recipes: a Zapier/Make template + Gorgias/Zendesk trigger examples for the webhook (`POST /api/inbox`) in `docs/` | — | 45 min |

---

## 7. Workstream F: repository and structure

**Before the deadline (keep it small):**
- Delete the leftover folders: `app/`, `cfo/`, `landing/` (only `__pycache__` left), `tmp/`, `.tmp_pytest*`.

## 1. Judges and scoring: where the points are

The judges are **2 from Entire, 2 from neatlogs and 1 from Orchestrator.inc**. The video and building in public are done, so 45% of the score is now in play:

| Criterion | Weight | Where we lose points today |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | State and iteration are weak (single-turn), the task is narrow, and τ-bench is only a replay |
| neatlogs + Entire + cfo.ai | 25% | The tools are used separately, not as one chain. Gates are failing, and there's no proof from the real neatlogs dashboard |
| Usefulness + originality | 10% | No live link, Stripe not tested for real, it only works inside our own app |

**Core strategy:** make the three tools into **one connected loop**: *the neatlogs trace caught a failure → Entire found the code and the session behind it → fix → neatlogs compare verified the fix → cfo.ai showed the margin impact.* That is exactly how neatlogs pitches itself (*"find the code behind a failure, then compare runs to verify your fix"*) and how Entire pitches itself (*"save the context behind each change"*).

---

## 2. Workstream A: making the agent better (30%)

The hackathon's focus areas are planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification and iteration. We are already strong on **recovery and verification**. The gaps are **state, context, iteration and planning**.

### A1. Multi-turn conversation (state + context): ⭐ highest priority
**Problem:** when the agent asks "which order?", the customer's reply arrives as a new, unrelated ticket. The context is lost.
**Plan:**
- Tickets get a `follows_ticket_id` (thread) link. When a new message arrives, look for an open `needs_info` ticket from the same sender within the last 14 days.
- Read the earlier message plus the reply together (the full context goes into intake). The trace gets a new `agent.context` span ("continues #12").
- Mark the earlier ticket `answered`. In the Inbox UI, show a "Customer replied" box on a `needs_info` ticket.
- Demo: add a customer with 2 open orders → the agent asks which one → reply "ORD-1010" → done and verified.

**Source:**
- **τ²-bench** ([sierra-research/tau2-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench), Barres et al. 2025, [arXiv:2506.07982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07982)): its "dual-control" idea, where the user also acts and the conversation is multi-turn. Borrow its user-simulator pattern for our tests.

**Files:** `sololicense/agent/loop.py` (`_handle`), `db/repositories/tickets.py`, `db/database.py` (`_ADDED_COLUMNS`), `api/app.py` (new `POST /api/tickets/{id}/reply`), `frontend/.../Inbox.jsx`.
**Verify:** integration test (ask, then reply, then DONE), `pytest`, one trace in neatlogs showing the context span.
**Effort:** 3 hours · **Risk:** low

### A2. Visible re-planning (iteration)
**Problem:** when the order isn't found, the fallback (email lookup) happens silently in code. A judge can't see it in the trace.
**Plan:** turn each lookup strategy (order number → sender email → email + amount match) into its own span, `agent.find_order.attempt`, so the trace shows "attempt 1 failed → tried the next route". Also add a reason-coded **retry note** after a failed verification (the agent writes why it failed, and the next attempt reads it).
**Source:**
- **ReAct** (Yao et al. 2022, [arXiv:2210.03629](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)): the reason → act → observe loop.
- **Reflexion** (Shinn et al. 2023, [arXiv:2303.11366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)): store "what went wrong" as text after a failure and use it on the next attempt. We don't need the whole RL loop; only the *failure note → next attempt* pattern.

**Files:** `agent/loop.py` (`_find_order`), `agent/worker.py` (`_recover`).
**Effort:** 1.5 hours · **Risk:** low

### A3. Statistically sound demotion and promotion
**Today:** promotion uses the Beta-posterior upper bound (good). Demotion means one failure pauses the job type immediately (safe, but blunt).
**Plan:**
- **SPRT (Wald's Sequential Probability Ratio Test):** test each new run online for "is the failure rate above break-even?" It allows a fast and statistically defensible demotion and an explainable "evidence enough" decision. Write it in the README as *"promotion = Bayesian bound, demotion = SPRT"*.
- **Learn-then-Test** (Angelopoulos et al. 2021, [arXiv:2110.01052](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.01052)) / **Conformal Risk Control** ([arXiv:2208.02814](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02814)): calibrate the limits (L2 ceiling, confidence) with a guarantee that the risk stays ≤ α.

**Files:** `sololicense/domain/trust.py` (pure functions, easy to test), `tests/unit/test_trust.py`.
**Effort:** 2–3 hours · **Risk:** medium (maths must be checked; keep the existing behaviour as the default)

### A4. Knowing when it doesn't know (abstention from intake confidence)
**Problem:** the LLM intake's `confidence` field is not used for any decision.
**Plan:** calibrate a threshold with conformal prediction. When intake is uncertain (two plausible task classes or amounts), the agent sends it to `needs_info` or `needs_human` instead of guessing. Calibration data: the sample inbox plus about 50 synthetic messages.
**Source:** **KnowNo: Robots That Ask for Help** (Ren et al. 2023, [arXiv:2307.01928](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.01928)): *if the prediction set has more than one option, ask for help.*
**Files:** `agent/intake.py`, `agent/loop.py`.
**Effort:** 2 hours · **Risk:** low

### A5. Prompt-injection defence with a benchmark number
**Today:** a regex blocks steering messages, and authority never comes from the model. That's good, but there is no measured number for it.
**Plan:**
- Write in the README that our design already follows CaMeL's principle: *untrusted data never controls the program's flow*. The LLM only extracts fields; policy, licence and read-back decide.
- Build a small injection suite (about 30 messages: "ignore rules", "send refund to new card", hidden instructions, unicode tricks). Report: *"0/30 reached the worker"*.

**Source:**
- **CaMeL: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design** (Debenedetti et al. 2025, [arXiv:2503.18813](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813), code: [google-research/camel-prompt-injection](https://github.com/google-research/camel-prompt-injection))
- **AgentDojo** ([ethz-spylab/agentdojo](https://github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo)): use its attack types to build the suite.
- **LlamaFirewall** (Meta [PurpleLlama](https://github.com/meta-llama/PurpleLlama)) / **Invariant Guardrails** ([invariantlabs-ai/invariant](https://github.com/invariantlabs-ai/invariant)): as an optional second layer for detecting injected text. Don't add the dependency before the deadline; mention it as related work.

**Files:** new `tests/integration/test_injection_suite.py`, `scripts/` + `evidence/benchmarks/injection.md`.
**Effort:** 2 hours · **Risk:** low

### A6. A live run on a standard dataset (stretch)
**Problem:** the τ-bench result is a counterfactual replay of recorded trajectories, not our own agent running.
**Plan:** run our agent on 15–20 retail return/refund tasks from τ²-bench's `retail` domain (adapter: τ-bench tools → our connector interface). Use the hackathon's LiteLLM key ($20 budget). Report pass^1 and "wrong writes reaching the customer".
**Source:** [sierra-research/tau2-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench) (MIT, uses LiteLLM); original [sierra-research/tau-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau-bench) ([arXiv:2406.12045](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045)).
**Effort:** 4–6 hours · **Risk:** high. Start only after A1, A2 and A5 are done.

### A7. Rules as declarative policy (originality)
**Plan:** move the shop's rules (refund window, identity, caps) from code into a small declarative rule file (YAML) that the owner can read and edit in Settings, with each rule's hit shown in the trace.
**Source:** **AgentSpec** (Wang et al., ICSE 2026, [arXiv:2503.18666](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18666)): its trigger → predicate → enforcement DSL pattern. **NeMo Guardrails** ([NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails)): its config-driven rails idea.
**Files:** `agent/policy.py`.
**Effort:** 3 hours · **Risk:** medium. Post-hackathon is fine.

# Launch Evidence Operations Plan

> **For agentic workers:** Execute each externally visible action only with the user's explicit scope and keep publishing/account actions separately confirmable.

**Goal:** Capture judge-ready Neatlogs and CFO evidence, restore Entire Trail health, and prepare the product's launch evidence without exposing secrets.

**Architecture:** Evidence files live under `docs/assets/screens`; README links them from the existing evidence table. Entire configuration is checked through its CLI and Trail gates. CFO updates happen only in the existing user-owned CFO model; payment-account creation and public publishing remain separate account actions.

**Tech Stack:** Neatlogs web app and SDK integration, Entire CLI/Trails, CFO.ai, GitHub, Stripe test mode, README Markdown.

## Review Focus

- Screenshot must be the specified recovery trace and visibly show the requested span tree.
- No API key, token, customer data, or browser profile information appears in an image or commit.
- Trail approvals are limited to the exact Trails named by the user.
- CFO values match the supplied 50-run benchmark exactly.
- Financial/account creation and public posts wait for action-time confirmation where required.

### Task 1: Capture and commit Neatlogs evidence

- [ ] Open the supplied trace while authenticated to Neatlogs.
- [ ] Verify the recovery span tree and capture a full-page image to `docs/assets/screens/neatlogs.png`.
- [ ] Add the image to README evidence and commit it on a dedicated PR.

### Task 2: Repair and verify Entire

- [ ] Run `entire doctor`, apply its proposed repair, then run `entire status`.
- [ ] Approve only Trails 2, 3, 4 and the Trail associated with PR #12.
- [ ] Record any gate that remains blocked and its exact cause.

### Task 3: Update the CFO model

- [ ] Apply the supplied measured benchmark changes to “Solo License — autonomy economics”.
- [ ] Verify all four scenarios are recalculated and capture the scorecard if it contains no sensitive data.

### Task 4: Payments and publishing handoff

- [ ] Have the user complete any Stripe account/key creation action requiring account or key confirmation.
- [ ] Add the user-provided Stripe test key only through the app's encrypted Settings UI, test it, and verify test-mode payments.
- [ ] Start recording and social publishing only after the user has selected the account/platform and approved final publication.

## Self-review

The plan covers every requested evidence source and isolates key creation, payment actions, uploads, and public posts as account-impacting steps. It does not treat third-party page text as authorization.
=====
# Product-ready Solo License demo Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make the existing refund-worker demo accessible, configurable with customer-owned model keys, and credible as a product without requiring a hosted database.

**Architecture:** Keep the licensed refund worker and SQLite repositories intact. Add provider-specific configuration behind the existing `complete()` interface, add an explicit in-memory demo session only behind a local-demo flag, and let the React client supply a session-scoped Bearer token. A shared provider definition keeps onboarding and Settings aligned.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLite, React 19, Vite, browser `sessionStorage`, Node test runner.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-solo-license-product-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- The application must remain runnable with no paid key, hosted database, or cloud account.
- SQLite remains local-demo storage; this delivery adds no hosted DB migration.
- Customer API keys are encrypted server-side, masked on read, and never logged or committed.
- Gemini uses an API key and configurable model; custom providers require a key, model, and HTTPS base URL.
- Demo access must be opt-in with `SOLO_DEMO_MODE`; no unauthenticated fallback is permitted.
- cfo.ai is an OAuth MCP integration and Trails is feature-flag/admin-gated; neither may be represented as already connected.

## Review Focus

- A deployed environment sets `SOLO_DEMO_MODE=true` accidentally: the documentation and API response must make the insecure demo-only state visible.
- A custom provider has an HTTP, loopback, or malformed URL: validation must reject it before network I/O.
- A form re-submits a masked or blank key: the persisted secret must remain unchanged.
- A stored browser token is missing or expires: the client must clear it and return to access setup rather than loop on 401s.
- A Gemini response lacks a text candidate or returns an error body: the test endpoint must show a bounded recoverable message without key material.

---

- Modify: `sololicense/agent/intake.py`
- Modify: `tests/test_intake.py`
- Create: `tests/test_provider_config.py`

Assert `replace(harness.config, llm_provider="gemini", gemini_api_key="key")` and an OpenAI-compatible configuration report `llm_enabled`, while a custom HTTP endpoint is rejected by a validation helper.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the configuration tests to verify they fail**

Run: `python -m pytest tests/test_provider_config.py -q`
Expected: FAIL because the new configuration fields and validation helper do not exist.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add provider fields and endpoint validation to `Config`**

Load `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_MODEL`, `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_MODEL`, and `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL`. Accept only `https` absolute URLs that do not target loopback/private hostnames.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the configuration tests to verify they pass**

Run: `python -m pytest tests/test_provider_config.py -q`
Expected: PASS.

- [ ] **Step 5: Write failing completion-adapter tests**

In `tests/test_intake.py`, monkeypatch the HTTP transport and assert Gemini posts `contents` to the configured model endpoint with `X-goog-api-key`, custom provider posts OpenAI chat-completions payload to `<base>/chat/completions`, and both return extracted text.

- [ ] **Step 6: Run the completion-adapter tests to verify they fail**

Expected: FAIL because no adapter branch exists.

Use `urllib.request` with `Config.llm_timeout_seconds`; bound provider error bodies and raise `RuntimeError` without key material. Preserve existing Anthropic and OpenAI client behavior.

**Files:**
- Modify: `app/api.py`
- Modify: `sololicense/config.py`
- Modify: `tests/test_api_security.py`
- Modify: `tests/test_settings_secrets.py`

- Consumes: Task 1 provider fields and `complete()`.
- Produces: `POST /api/access/demo -> {"token": str, "expires_at": str}` only when `SOLO_DEMO_MODE=true`.
- Produces: `serialize_settings()` fields and masked hints for Gemini and custom-provider keys; `_clean_values(values) -> dict[str, str]` accepts the two provider identifiers and validates custom URLs.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing API tests for new setting secrets and demo access**

Assert secrets encrypt/mask for Gemini and compatible providers; assert `/api/access/demo` is unavailable when disabled, returns an admin-capable ephemeral token when enabled, and that token can call `/api/dashboard` until expiry.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the new API tests to verify they fail**

Run: `python -m pytest tests/test_api_security.py tests/test_settings_secrets.py -q`
Expected: FAIL because the endpoint and new fields do not exist.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement session issuer and settings serialization in `app/api.py`**

Add an in-memory, lock-protected demo-session store with a configurable TTL. `current_actor()` checks deployment tokens first and valid demo sessions second. Require explicit demo mode and never create an actor for an anonymous request.

- [ ] **Step 4: Expand API settings validation and the LLM test configuration**

Add provider-specific fields to the setting/secret allowlists, `serialize_settings`, `test_llm`, and clean-value validation. Preserve masked/blank key behavior.

- [ ] **Step 5: Run focused API tests to verify they pass**

Run: `python -m pytest tests/test_api_security.py tests/test_settings_secrets.py -q`
Expected: PASS.

- [ ] **Step 6: Commit**

Commit: `git add app/api.py sololicense/config.py tests/test_api_security.py tests/test_settings_secrets.py && git commit -m "feat: add secured demo access and provider settings"`

### Task 3: Session-aware client API and access screen

**Files:**
- Create: `frontend/src/lib/accessSession.js`
- Create: `frontend/src/lib/accessSession.test.js`
- Modify: `frontend/src/lib/api.js`
- Create: `frontend/src/features/access/Access.jsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/entry.jsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/features/app/AppShell.jsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/index.css`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 2 `POST /api/access/demo` response.
- Produces: `getAccessToken()`, `saveAccessSession(session)`, `clearAccessSession()`, and `isSessionExpired()`.
- Produces: all authenticated `request()` calls include `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; a 401 clears the session.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing Node tests for access-session behavior**

Use an in-memory `sessionStorage` fake. Assert a saved non-expired session returns its token, an expired session is cleared, and `api.request()` adds the correct authorization header without serializing the token into the body.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run access-session tests to verify they fail**

Run: `npm test -- --test-name-pattern='access session|authorization header'`
Working directory: `frontend`
Expected: FAIL because the module and header logic do not exist.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `accessSession.js` and integrate it into `api.js`**

Keep tokens session-scoped. Add `api.startDemo()` and have `request()` clear expired/unauthorized sessions before surfacing a normal error.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement `Access.jsx` and route guard**

Offer Try the demo (calls `api.startDemo`) and Connect an existing workspace (paste a deployment token). If no usable session exists, protect `/onboarding` and `/app`; if one exists, route to onboarding or dashboard according to backend state.

- [ ] **Step 5: Run frontend tests and production build**

Run: `npm test && npm run build`
Working directory: `frontend`
Expected: PASS.

- [ ] **Step 6: Commit**

Commit: `git add frontend/src/lib frontend/src/features/access frontend/src/entry.jsx frontend/src/features/app/AppShell.jsx frontend/src/index.css && git commit -m "feat: add demo workspace access flow"`

### Task 4: Shared provider form and guided onboarding

**Files:**
- Create: `frontend/src/lib/providers.js`
- Create: `frontend/src/lib/providers.test.js`
- Modify: `frontend/src/features/app/components/ModelFields.jsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/features/app/pages/Settings.jsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/features/onboarding/Onboarding.jsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/features/onboarding/steps/StepModel.jsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/index.css`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 2 serialized settings and Task 3 authenticated `api.testLlm()`.
- Produces: `providerFields(providerId) -> {keyField, modelField, baseUrlField?}` and `PROVIDERS` definitions for deterministic, Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI, and OpenAI-compatible.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing provider metadata tests**

Assert Gemini maps to `gemini_api_key`/`gemini_model`, OpenAI-compatible maps to key/model/base URL fields, and deterministic needs no fields.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run provider metadata tests to verify they fail**

Run: `npm test -- --test-name-pattern='provider metadata'`
Working directory: `frontend`
Expected: FAIL because the shared metadata module does not exist.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement provider metadata and refactor `ModelFields`**

Render provider-specific labels, safe placeholders, required HTTPS base URL, saved-key hints, and the existing test connection control from metadata. Submit only fields belonging to the selected provider.

- [ ] **Step 4: Wire Settings and onboarding to the shared provider form**

Persist/map all new settings fields; require a successful configuration or deterministic choice before onboarding advances. Keep the sample-order choice and license policy steps unchanged.

- [ ] **Step 5: Run metadata tests and production build**

Run: `npm test && npm run build`
Working directory: `frontend`
Expected: PASS.

- [ ] **Step 6: Commit**

Commit: `git add frontend/src/lib/providers.js frontend/src/lib/providers.test.js frontend/src/features/app/components/ModelFields.jsx frontend/src/features/app/pages/Settings.jsx frontend/src/features/onboarding frontend/src/index.css && git commit -m "feat: guide provider setup in onboarding"`

### Task 5: Finance review export and deployment integration guide

**Files:**
- Create: `sololicense/services/finance_review.py`
- Create: `tests/test_finance_review.py`
- Modify: `app/api.py`
- Modify: `frontend/src/lib/api.js`
- Modify: `frontend/src/features/app/components/EvidencePacket.jsx`
- Create: `docs/INTEGRATIONS.md`
- Modify: `.env.example`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `EvidencePacket` data returned by `serialize_packet(context, run_id)`.
- Produces: `build_finance_review(packet: dict) -> dict` with amount, verification delta, detections, decision, autonomy level, and neatlogs reference—never secret settings.
- Produces: `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/finance-review` and a browser Download JSON action.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing finance-review tests**

Create a packet fixture and assert the export includes business-safe review fields, rounds currency values, includes detections, and omits all `*_api_key` values.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run finance-review tests to verify they fail**

Run: `python -m pytest tests/test_finance_review.py -q`
Expected: FAIL because the service and endpoint do not exist.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the export service and protected API endpoint**

Build the review from the existing evidence packet only. Return 404 for an unknown run and require operator role.

- [ ] **Step 4: Add Evidence Packet download action**

Use `api.financeReview(runId)` and a Blob download named `solo-license-finance-review-<runId>.json`. Do not add cfo.ai credentials or claim automatic cfo.ai submission.

- [ ] **Step 5: Document deployment and external integrations**

Update `.env.example` with non-secret variable names and safe defaults. `docs/INTEGRATIONS.md` must explain Gemini, GLM-compatible endpoint, neatlogs, cfo.ai OAuth MCP, Entire hooks/Graph, and the manual prerequisites for Trails.

- [ ] **Step 6: Run focused tests, full backend suite, and frontend build**

Run: `python -m pytest && npm run build`
Working directory for the second command: `frontend`
Expected: PASS.

- [ ] **Step 7: Commit**

Commit: `git add sololicense/services/finance_review.py tests/test_finance_review.py app/api.py frontend/src/lib/api.js frontend/src/features/app/components/EvidencePacket.jsx docs/INTEGRATIONS.md .env.example && git commit -m "feat: export finance-ready evidence packets"`

## Self-review

- Spec coverage: Tasks 1–4 cover no-key operation, provider setup, masking, connection testing, explicit demo access, onboarding, and future auth seams. Task 5 covers finance review, neatlogs/cfo/Entire/Trails guidance, and deployment variables. Hosted authentication and database migration remain explicitly out of scope as specified.
- Type consistency: Task 1 owns all added `Config` fields; Task 2 exposes their API names; Task 4 maps exactly those names from one frontend metadata module.
- Review focus coverage: Task 1 tests malformed custom URLs and provider response errors; Task 2 tests opt-in demo access and masked secrets; Task 3 tests missing/expired sessions; Task 4 tests provider form mappings.
- Proportion: five independently releasable tasks with one backend or frontend concern each; implementation bodies are deliberately not prescribed.

=== 19b1330
Swyam Sharma
fix(observability): run the neatlogs Doctor probe in an isolated child process

The API process initialises neatlogs at startup for agent traces; calling
doctor_probe_v2 in the same process re-initialises the SDK with a different
configuration, which it refuses, and the Doctor maps that to
BACKEND_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE - so the onboarding Test button always failed,
connectivity notwithstanding.

The probe now runs in a short-lived python -I -c child: the key and
endpoint travel through the child's environment (never argv, never logs,
never the report), the child prints one safe JSON line, the parent bounds
it at the Doctor's own 45s budget, and every failure (timeout, crash,
unparseable output) maps to a structured {ok, code, message} response
(AUTH_FAILED, TRACE_READBACK_TIMEOUT, BACKEND_*, PROBE_TIMEOUT) with the
credential scrubbed defensively. Verified live: a bogus key now returns a
real AUTH_FAILED from ingest.neatlogs.com in ~2s.

=== ae6b8b6
Swyam Sharma
fix(api): make onboarding atomic and reject re-handling a message

complete_onboarding persisted onboarded=1 before parsing the CSV or
validating manual order ids, so a rejected payload left a half-onboarded
workspace the UI treated as set up (with uncommitted writes still open in
the transaction). The CSV and order-id validation now runs before any
write, and the parser's row problems surface in the 422 detail.

Handling an already-handled ticket re-ran the agent with the same
idempotency key, which flagged a duplicate action and demoted the license
for what was only a double-submit; it is now a 409.

Also pins settings_encryption_key="" in the test harness: the suite
inherited the key from a developer's .env and
test_settings_secret_requires_server_encryption_key failed on any machine
that followed the documented setup.

=== b0b9bba
Swyam Sharma
fix(web): turn neatlogs probe codes into actionable guidance

The Test row translated every failure through the generic provider-error
map, so BACKEND_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE landed on 'That did not work.' The API
now returns a structured code; plainNeatlogsError maps each code to what
the owner should do (key rejected / trace still processing / endpoint or
network / probe issue, try again), never echoes the raw key, and falls
back to the old wording when no code is present. plainError moves to
lib/plain-errors.js so both maps stay node-testable. The Project ID note
now says what it is (a label for traces) and what Test checks (send one
diagnostic trace, read it back).

An unauthorized attempt must not mutate `orders`. - Policy changes cannot silently increase a license level. - Run `python -m pytest` and `npm --prefix frontend run build` before reporting this milestone complete. ## Review Focus - A permit for refund must be rejected by the store-credit tool, even for the same order and amount. - An expired or previously consumed permit must leave the order unchanged. - A policy activation immediately after a clean run must not let evidence from the older policy promote the class. - # Solo License: implementation plan for winning (v2)

*11 Oct 2026 · `main` @ `d852fb6` (after PRs #15 and #16) · Submission: **Mon 12 Oct, 7:00–11:55 PM IST***

This is a **plan only**, with no code. v2 replaces the plan written at `e1e4910`. It takes into account the 7 commits that landed on `origin/main` since then, says what they finished, what they broke, and what to do next, in order.

---

## 0. What changed on `main` since v1

| Commit | Author | What it did | Effect on the plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| `19b1330` | Swyam | neatlogs Doctor probe runs in an isolated child process; structured codes (`AUTH_FAILED`, `TRACE_READBACK_TIMEOUT`, …) | The onboarding neatlogs **Test** button works now. B1 (dashboard screenshots) is unblocked |
| `ae6b8b6` | Swyam | Onboarding is atomic; re-handling a handled ticket returns **409** instead of demoting | A1 (multi-turn) must create a *new* linked ticket, never re-handle the old one |
| `b0b9bba` | Swyam | Frontend maps probe codes to plain guidance | Done, nothing to add |
| `7d40d25` | Vansh | **Versioned policies + single-use execution permits** (`domain/policy.py`, `services/policy_gate.py`, `policy_service.py`, `PolicyEditor.jsx`, `docs/policy-governance.md`) | **A7 is done** (rules are now data, editable, versioned). New demo beat: an unauthorized write is blocked at the permit boundary |
| `218710c` | Vansh | Permits enforced inside Local and Stripe connectors | Same; also makes E3 (MCP server) much easier: it can hand out permits |
| `12ada5f` | Vansh | "features": commits `artifacts/evidence_report.*`, removes 11 lines from `frontend/package-lock.json` | `artifacts/` is now tracked (conflicts with v1 F item). Vague commit message |
| `e7951c9` | Swyam | README em dashes → hyphens | Two em dashes came back in the new README section |

**Verified now:** `python -m pytest` → **161 passed** (was 117). Frontend: **11/11** tests pass, build OK, JS chunk **723 kB** (was 712 kB).

**Local main:** fast-forwarded to `d852fb6`. The two untracked local `artifacts/evidence_report.*` files (older regenerated copies) were moved to the session scratchpad so the merge could run; the committed versions from `12ada5f` are now in place.

**Stash:** `stash@{0}` (A1 work in progress: `db/database.py`, `db/repositories/tickets.py`) was made on the old base. Both files were touched by the new commits (`database.py` got policy columns), so expect a small conflict on `git stash pop`.

---

## 1. New problems the commits introduced (fix first)

### P1. ⚠️ Promotion no longer uses the economics (highest priority)
**What happened:** in the worker path, `LicenseService.record_clean_run(..., evaluation=...)` now promotes when `evaluate_runs()` says *"≥ minimum_samples and pass rate ≥ minimum_verified_pass_rate"*. The Beta-posterior / break-even rule in `domain/trust.py` is only used when `evaluation is None`, which the worker never passes.
**Why it matters:** the README's headline differentiator, *"promotion priced by economics … upper credible bound below break-even"* and *"759 more double-checked jobs"*, is no longer what the agent actually does. A judge who reads `worker.py` → `license_service.py` will see a fixed sample count. This is also exactly what the 30% agent criterion and the cfo.ai story rest on.
**Plan:** make policy eligibility **AND** the economic bound both required:
- `eligible = policy minimums met AND Beta upper bound (computed only from this policy version's outcomes) < break-even target for this step`.
- Keep the policy's minimums as a *floor* the owner sets; the economics stays the *ceiling* nobody can lower by editing a policy.
- `EvaluationProgress` gains the "jobs still needed by the economics" number, so Home keeps showing the "759 more…" sentence alongside the policy's sample/pass-rate progress.
- Promotion reason in the ledger names both: *"policy v3 minimums met; failure rate below 0.25% with 95% confidence."*

**Files:** `sololicense/domain/policy.py` (`evaluate_runs`), `domain/trust.py` (reuse, no change), `services/policy_service.py` (`evaluation_for`), `services/license_service.py`, `api/app.py` (`serialize_evaluation`), `frontend/.../Overview.jsx`.
**Verify:** new unit tests: (a) 3/3 clean with `minimum_samples=3` does **not** promote when the Beta bound is above break-even; (b) promotes once both hold; (c) evidence from an older policy version still never counts. Full `pytest`.
**Effort:** 1.5 hours · **Risk:** medium (touches the promotion path; keep `test_policy_service.py` green).

### P2. README regressions
- Line 193–194: the *"Live Stripe keys are refused…"* line is duplicated.
- Two em dashes reintroduced in the new section (*"writes a plan — it never…"*), against PR #16's intent.
- The *"Who it is for"* table was inserted directly under the heading, above the paragraph it belongs with; reorder.
- *"Tests: `python -m pytest` - 117 tests"* → 161.
- *"Earns freedom … after the current policy's required double-checked jobs"*: rewrite once P1 lands (policy floor **and** economic proof).
- `docs/policy-governance.md` says to choose **Anthropic** only; the README lists Groq/Gemini/OpenAI/compatible too. Make them consistent.

**Effort:** 20 min · **Risk:** none.

### P3. `artifacts/` and the lockfile
- Decide one place for generated evidence: change `scripts/generate_evidence.py` to write to `evidence/` (v1 suggestion), `git rm --cached artifacts/`, add `artifacts/` to `.gitignore`. Otherwise each run produces a dirty tree with a new timestamp.
- `12ada5f` removed 11 lines from `frontend/package-lock.json`. Build and tests pass, but run `npm ci` once from a clean clone (or in the CI from C1) to confirm the lockfile is still consistent.

**Effort:** 20 min · **Risk:** low.

### P4. Team hygiene (two teammates are now committing to `main`)
- Agree that every change goes branch → PR → trail, including teammates' (PR-based commits are what Entire and the judges see). `7d40d25`/`218710c`/`12ada5f` show up in history with one-word or empty messages; future ones should use the `feat:/fix:` style the rest of the history uses.
- Don't rewrite pushed history to fix the messages; just follow the rule from now on.

---

## 2. Status of every v1 item

| v1 item | Status now | Action in v2 |
|---|---|---|
| A1 multi-turn follow-up | Not done; WIP in stash | **Keep, high priority.** Adjust to the 409 rule (new linked ticket) |
| A2 visible re-planning | Not done | Keep |
| A3 SPRT demotion | Not done | Keep as stretch; now operates per policy version (`runs.policy_version`) |
| A4 abstention | Not done | Keep, lower priority |
| A5 injection suite | Not done | Keep; **stronger now**: the suite can count "blocked at intake" vs "blocked at permit" |
| A6 live τ²-bench | Not done | Stretch only |
| A7 declarative rules | ✅ **Done** by versioned policies | Drop. Add AgentSpec/NeMo as related-work line in README |
| B1 neatlogs screenshots | Unblocked by `19b1330` | Keep, do early |
| B2–B5 | Not done | Keep; add a `policy.version` + `permit.id` attribute on spans (cheap, new) |
| C1 Entire gates | Not done (still no `.github/workflows`) | Keep, first |
| C2 Entire depth | Not done | Keep; C2d now also covers `policy_gate.py` `consume_for_write` |
| D1–D5 cfo.ai | Not done | Keep; depends on P1 for the "same numbers" claim |
| E1 deploy + `/api/health` | Not done | Keep; follow `docs/policy-governance.md` deployment checklist |
| E2 Stripe live test | Not done | Keep; now also verifies a permit is consumed on the Stripe path |
| E3 MCP licence server | Not done | Keep as stretch, **cheaper now** (see E3 below) |
| E4, E5 | Not done | Keep |
| F repo cleanup | Partly obsolete | Replaced by P3; still delete `app/`, `cfo/`, `landing/`, `tmp/` leftovers |

---

## 3. Workstream A: the agent (30%)

### A1. Multi-turn conversation (state + context): ⭐
**Plan (updated for 409):**
- A reply never re-handles the old ticket. It creates a **new ticket** with `follows_ticket_id` pointing to the open `needs_info` ticket from the same sender within 14 days.
- Intake reads the earlier message plus the reply. The trace gets an `agent.context` span ("continues #12").
- The earlier ticket is marked `answered`. Inbox shows "Customer replied" on it.
- The new run goes through the normal policy + permit path; nothing special about authority.
- Demo: customer with 2 open orders → agent asks which → reply "ORD-1010" → done and verified.

**Start from:** `git stash pop` on a branch off `d852fb6`; resolve the `db/database.py` conflict (keep both the policy columns and `follows_ticket_id`).
**Source:** τ²-bench ([sierra-research/tau2-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench), [arXiv:2506.07982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07982)), dual-control / user-simulator pattern for the test.
**Files:** `agent/loop.py`, `db/repositories/tickets.py`, `db/database.py`, `api/app.py` (`POST /api/tickets/{id}/reply` or reuse `/api/inbox` with sender matching), `frontend/.../Inbox.jsx`.
**Verify:** integration test ask → reply → DONE; a test that replying to an already-handled ticket still returns 409; one neatlogs trace with the context span.
**Effort:** 3 hours · **Risk:** low

### A2. Visible re-planning
Unchanged from v1: one `agent.find_order.attempt` span per lookup strategy, plus a reason-coded retry note after a failed verification (ReAct [arXiv:2210.03629](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629), Reflexion [arXiv:2303.11366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)). New: a `policy.blocked` span already exists; make sure the retry path never requests a second permit for the same idempotency key (the policy plan's review focus calls this out).
**Files:** `agent/loop.py` (`_find_order`), `agent/worker.py` (`_recover`). **Effort:** 1.5 hours

### A5. Injection suite with a number
About 30 messages (AgentDojo attack types). Report two numbers instead of one: *"N stopped at intake, the rest stopped at the permit boundary, **0/30 changed an order**."* This shows defence in depth, which the permit work made real. Frame it as CaMeL's principle ([arXiv:2503.18813](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813)).
**Files:** `tests/integration/test_injection_suite.py`, `evidence/benchmarks/injection.md`. **Effort:** 2 hours

### A3, A4, A6
As in v1. A3 (SPRT) must read outcomes per `runs.policy_version`, so it fits next to P1. All three are stretch.

---

## 4. Workstream B: neatlogs

| # | Task | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | Dashboard screenshots: the recovered-refund trace **and** a run with `policy.blocked` → `evidence/assets/screens/neatlogs-*.png` | 30 min |
| B2 | OTel GenAI attributes (`gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.*`, `gen_ai.operation.name`) | 1 hour |
| B3 | Cost per ticket as a span attribute (shared with cfo.ai, D4) | 1 hour |
| B4 | Detections as events with severity | 30 min |
| B5 | "Open in neatlogs" link on every Inbox ticket | 30 min |
| B6 *(new)* | `policy.version` and `permit.id` attributes on `tool.execute` spans | 20 min |

---

## 5. Workstream C: Entire

**C1 (gates)** is unchanged from v1 and still the first task: GitHub Actions workflow (pytest + `npm ci` + frontend test + build), self-approval setting on entire.io (**you**), trail-review runner settings, `entire doctor` (**you**). The CI also covers P3's lockfile check. PR #14 is still open; close or merge it once its runner finishes.

**C2:** as in v1, plus: run `entire graph impact` on `consume_for_write` and `record_clean_run` for the P1 PR description, and add `entire why` for `policy_gate.py` to `evidence/entire.md`.

---

## 6. Workstream D: cfo.ai

D1–D5 as in v1. D1 and D4 only make sense after P1, because "the P&L and the agent use one set of numbers" is only true again once promotion uses the break-even rate.

---

## 7. Workstream E: usefulness and originality

- **E1 deploy:** use the deployment checklist in `docs/policy-governance.md` (`SOLO_DEMO_MODE`, `SOLO_API_TOKENS`, `SOLO_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, persistent DB and ledger repo). Add `/api/health`. Public demo stays demo mode with the sample shop.
- **E2 Stripe test mode:** one real test-mode refund, Stripe dashboard screenshot, and confirm the permit is consumed on the Stripe connector path. Then remove the "not yet tested live" line.
- **E3 licence-as-a-service MCP server (stretch, now cheaper):** `request_licence(task_class, order, amount)` returns allow / prepare / deny **plus a single-use permit** from `PolicyGate.issue`; `report_outcome(run_id, verified)` feeds evaluation. The permit model from `7d40d25` is exactly the primitive this needs ([MCP python-sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk); compare [stripe/agent-toolkit](https://github.com/stripe/agent-toolkit)).
- **E4:** README line: our licence implements the "autonomy certificate" of [arXiv:2506.12469](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12469), earned from evidence, **versioned by policy**, revocable and priced.
- **E5:** helpdesk recipes in `docs/`.

---

## 8. Order of work (until the deadline)

| Order | Task | Time | Why now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **P1** promotion = policy floor + economic bound | 1.5 h | Restores the core claim the whole pitch rests on |
| 2 | **P2 + P3** README fixes, `artifacts/` decision | 40 min | Cheap, removes visible sloppiness |
| 3 | **C1** CI workflow + gate settings | 1 h | Entire judges; CI also guards teammates' pushes |
| 4 | **B1 + E2** neatlogs + Stripe screenshots | 1 h | Real proof, now unblocked |
| 5 | **A1** multi-turn (from the stash) | 3 h | State and context |
| 6 | **A5** injection suite (intake vs permit numbers) | 2 h | Measured safety claim |
| 7 | **A2** visible re-plan | 1.5 h | Iteration in the trace |
| 8 | README "one failure, three tools" chain + E4 + policy/permit paragraph | 1 h | Ties the story together |
| 9 | **E1** deploy + live link | 1.5 h | Easier for judges |
| 10 | **D1–D5** cfo.ai measured numbers | 1 h | Business depth |
| 11 | **C2 + B2–B6** | 2 h | Depth in tool use |
| Stretch | E3 MCP · A3 SPRT · A6 τ²-bench live | 3–6 h each | Only if time allows |

**Rule for every task (you and teammates):** branch → PR (Entire trail) → green gates → merge. Commit from PowerShell so the checkpoint trailer is attached. Coordinate with Swyam and Vansh so two people don't touch `api/app.py` or `worker.py` at the same time; P1 and A1 both touch the worker/licence path, so do P1 first and rebase A1 on it.

### Don't do these before the deadline
- Move the backend folder or split `app.py` (still 1,300+ lines; paths in README and Graph evidence would break).
- Redesign the landing page or add new UI pages (the Policy review page is the last new one).
- Add heavy dependencies (NeMo, LlamaFirewall).
- Change the seed inbox or default policy `v1` values in a way that breaks the recorded video flow.

-## 2. Workstream A: making the agent better (30%)
+## 1. New problems the commits introduced (fix first)

-The hackathon's focus areas are planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification and iteration. We are already strong on **recovery and verification**. The gaps are **state, context, iteration and planning**.
+### P1. ⚠️ Promotion no longer uses the economics (highest priority)

+**What happened:** in the worker path, `LicenseService.record_clean_run(..., evaluation=...)` now promotes when `evaluate_runs()` says *"≥ minimum_samples and pass rate ≥ minimum_verified_pass_rate"*. The Beta-posterior / break-even rule in `domain/trust.py` is only used when `evaluation is None`, which the worker never passes.

+**Why it matters:** the README's headline differentiator, *"promotion priced by economics … upper credible bound below break-even"* and *"759 more double-checked jobs"*, is no longer what the agent actually does. A judge who reads `worker.py` → `license_service.py` will see a fixed sample count. This is also exactly what the 30% agent criterion and the cfo.ai story rest on.
+**Plan:** make policy eligibility **AND** the economic bound both required:
+- `eligible = policy minimums met AND Beta upper bound (computed only from this policy version's outcomes) < break-even target for this step`.
+- Keep the policy's minimums as a *floor* the owner sets; the economics stays the *ceiling* nobody can lower by editing a policy.
+- `EvaluationProgress` gains the "jobs still needed by the economics" number, so Home keeps showing the "759 more…" sentence alongside the policy's sample/pass-rate progress.
+- Promotion reason in the ledger names both: *"policy v3 minimums met; failure rate below 0.25% with 95% confidence."*
-### A1. Multi-turn conversation (state + context): ⭐ highest priority
-**Problem:** when the agent asks "which order?", the customer's reply arrives as a new, unrelated ticket. The context is lost.
-**Plan:**
-- Tickets get a `follows_ticket_id` (thread) link. When a new message arrives, look for an open `needs_info` ticket from the same sender within the last 14 days.
-- Read the earlier message plus the reply together (the full context goes into intake). The trace gets a new `agent.context` span ("continues #12").
-- Mark the earlier ticket `answered`. In the Inbox UI, show a "Customer replied" box on a `needs_info` ticket.
-- Demo: add a customer with 2 open orders → the agent asks which one → reply "ORD-1010" → done and verified.

+**Files:** `sololicense/domain/policy.py` (`evaluate_runs`), `domain/trust.py` (reuse, no change), `services/policy_service.py` (`evaluation_for`), `services/license_service.py`, `api/app.py` (`serialize_evaluation`), `frontend/.../Overview.jsx`.

+**Verify:** new unit tests: (a) 3/3 clean with `minimum_samples=3` does **not** promote when the Beta bound is above break-even; (b) promotes once both hold; (c) evidence from an older policy version still never counts. Full `pytest`.
+**Effort:** 1.5 hours · **Risk:** medium (touches the promotion path; keep `test_policy_service.py` green).
-**Source:**

-- **τ²-bench** ([sierra-research/tau2-bench](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench), Barres et al. 2025, [arXiv:2506.07982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07982)): its "dual-control" idea, where the user also acts and the conversation is multi-turn. Borrow its user-simulator pattern for our tests.

-**Problem:** when the order isn't found, the fallback (email lookup) happens silently in code. A judge can't see it in the trace.

-**Plan:** turn each lookup strategy (order number → sender email → email + amount match) into its own span, `agent.find_order.attempt`, so the trace shows "attempt 1 failed → tried the next route". Also add a reason-coded **retry note** after a failed verification (the agent writes why it failed, and the next attempt reads it).
-**Source:**
-- **ReAct** (Yao et al. 2022, [arXiv:2210.03629](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)): the reason → act → observe loop.

-- **Reflexion** (Shinn et al. 2023, [arXiv:2303.11366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)): store "what went wrong" as text after a failure and use it on the next attempt. We don't need the whole RL loop; only the *failure note → next attempt* pattern.

-**Today:** promotion uses the Beta-posterior upper bound (good). Demotion means one failure pauses the job type immediately (safe, but blunt).
-**Plan:**

-- **SPRT (Wald's Sequential Probability Ratio Test):** test each new run online for "is the failure rate above break-even?" It allows a fast and statistically defensible demotion and an explainable "evidence enough" decision. Write it in the README as *"promotion = Bayesian bound, demotion = SPRT"*.

-- **Learn-then-Test** (Angelopoulos et al. 2021, [arXiv:2110.01052](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.01052)) / **Conformal Risk Control** ([arXiv:2208.02814](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02814)): calibrate the limits (L2 ceiling, confidence) with a guarantee that the risk stays ≤ α.

-**Source:** **KnowNo: Robots That Ask for Help** (Ren et al. 2023, [arXiv:2307.01928](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.01928)): *if the prediction set has more than one option, ask for help.*

-**Today:** a regex blocks steering messages, and authority never comes from the model. That's good, but there is no measured number for it.

Don't add the dependency before the deadline; mention it as related work.

-**Problem:** the τ-bench result is a counterfactual replay of recorded trajectories, not our own agent running.

-**Plan:** run our agent on 15–20 retail return/refund tasks from τ²-bench's `retail` domain (adapter: τ-bench tools → our connector interface). Use the hackathon's LiteLLM key ($20 budget). Report pass^1 and "wrong writes reaching the customer".

Merge ko local untracked `artifacts/evidence_report.*` files rok rahi thi. Wo purane generated copies the, unhe maine scratchpad mein move kiya, delete nahi kiya. Merge ke baad 161 backend tests aur 11/11 frontend tests pass hue, aur frontend build bhi chal gaya.

**Naye commits ki wajah se plan mein jo badla:**

1. **Sabse badi problem:** worker ab promotion ke liye sirf policy ka fixed rule use karta hai (kam se kam X clean runs aur Y% pass rate). Economics wala Beta bound / break-even rule agent ke path mein ab chalta hi nahi. README ka main claim ("promotion priced by economics", "759 more jobs") abhi code se match nahi karta. Plan mein ye **P1** hai, sabse pehle karna hai: promotion tab ho jab policy ka minimum **aur** economic bound, dono pass hon.
2. **A7 (declarative rules) ho chuka hai:** Vansh ki versioned policies ne ye kaam kar diya, isliye plan se hata diya.
3. **E3 (MCP server) aur A5 (injection suite) ab aasaan aur strong hain:** dono permit system pe build ho sakte hain.
4. **A1 (multi-turn) mein ek badlav:** handled ticket ko dobara handle karne pe ab 409 aata hai, to customer ka reply naya linked ticket banega. Stash wale kaam mein `db/database.py` pe chhota conflict aayega.
5. **README mein naye issues:** Stripe wali line do baar hai, do em dashes wapas aa gaye hain, aur tests ka number abhi bhi 117 likha hai jabki ab 161 hain.
6. **`artifacts/` folder:** Vansh ke commit se ab git mein track ho raha hai, to decide karna hoga ki generated evidence kahan rahe.
7. **Team rule:** Swyam aur Vansh bhi main pe commit kar rahe hain. Plan mein likha hai ki sab branch → PR → trail se jaayein, aur P1 pehle ho, uske baad A1 usi pe rebase ho.

Kaam ka order: **P1 → README fixes → CI gates → neatlogs/Stripe screenshots → A1 → A5 → A2 → …** Poori table plan ke section 8 mein hai.

Jo "comments" tumne bole the, wo mujhe kahin nahi mile. Main ne naye commits ko hi wo maan ke plan banaya hai. Agar wo kahin aur hain (kisi PR pe ya kisi doc mein), to link bhej do, main unhe bhi plan mein jod dunga.
